A local decision with that reach seems to deserve more scrutiny than a routine contract item usually receives.

I hope you will support removing the readers around {{shortName}} and approving none to replace them. Would you tell me your position?

subject: One prediction I feel confident about
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

I cannot tell you how the plate archive will be used a decade from now. Nobody can, and I would not trust anyone who claimed otherwise, myself included.

What seems predictable is that it will be larger. Every day the readers near {{shortName}} operate, the record of who was outside which building gets longer, and each addition is permanent in a way the surrounding policy is not.

Decisions under uncertainty usually favor the option that leaves fewer doors open for other people to walk through. Here that seems to mean collecting less.

So I am asking, as a student here, for removal around campus and no new installations. If you see the uncertainty differently, I would like to hear how. Either way, a statement of your position would be useful.

subject: A records question more than a camera question
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Discussion of plate readers tends to focus on the hardware, which seems to me the least interesting part. Cameras are cheap and replaceable. Archives are the durable object, and the questions worth asking are records questions: how long, who may search, under what authority, and what happens when the answers change.

Applied around {{shortName}}, those questions have no public answers that I can find. That alone gives me pause, since a record of attendance is being produced whether or not anyone has settled how it should be governed.

Governing it well looks harder to me than not producing it.

So I hope you will support removal of the readers around campus with no new ones approved, and I would like to know your position. I am a student writing for myself.

subject: Weekly attendance at a congregation is now recorded
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Congregations meet on a schedule, in the same place, with largely the same people, which makes them unusually legible to a system that logs plates by time and location.

Nothing about that requires anyone to be interested in a particular congregation. Legibility is a property of regular attendance, and a plate archive near {{shortName}} captures regularity better than it captures anything else.

What follows is a list, held indefinitely, of who was there most weeks. Nobody had to request it, and nobody has to justify keeping it. That is the shape of the thing that bothers me.

I am a student here and I would like the readers removed around campus with no new ones approved. Please tell me whether that is a position you would take, and if not, how you would answer the point.

subject: This binds people who are not here yet
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Students arriving in {{city}} some years from now will inherit whatever the council decides about this, and they will inherit the accumulated reads as well. None of them has any say in it, and by the time they arrive the arrangement will look settled rather than chosen.

That is how programs like this become permanent, as far as I can tell. Each year of collection makes removal look more like a disruption and less like a correction.

Breaking the pattern seems easier now than it will be later.

So I hope you will support taking the readers out around {{shortName}} and approving no new ones. Would you tell me whether you could support it, and if not, what would need to be true?

subject: A last word on the readers around campus
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

You may have received several letters on this, so I will add only the point I think carries the most weight.

A record of where a car stopped is a record of what a person attended. That record is kept whether or not anyone intends to read it, and it stays available long after the reason for collecting it has passed. Knowing it exists changes how people behave, and it changes most for those already under closer watch than the rest of us.

Nothing in that worry depends on anyone in {{city}} acting in bad faith.

So my request is the plain one: I would like the plate readers around {{shortName}} removed and no new ones installed. I would be grateful for your position, and for a reply either way. Thank you for reading a student's letter.
